subject: Data handshake & traceability — routing, subprocessors, and delete guarantees
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@solara.health>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Team <legal@solara.health>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Q: where does request data actually run / move?

Vanessa — thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to procurement, our security folks asked for a short written explanation of where inference requests are executed and who (which subprocessors) sees metadata and any transient data in-flight. Specifically: 

- If we route to an EU-only region, can you confirm no hops to US-based infra occur during inference?
- Which subprocessors are involved in routing, autoscaling, and logging for private/dedicated vs hosted?
- What is Redwood's guaranteed timeline for deletion of transient request data and cached KV prefixes after a customer requests deletion?

Can you provide a brief mapping and any evidence artifacts (SOC2 docs, region map)? We do not need legal language yet — just technical traceability for our engineering and security teams.

Thanks,
Alex Monroe
Head of Platform Security
Solara Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@solara.health>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does request data actually run / move?

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short region map and a one-page summary to start (redwood_regions_map.pdf). High-level answers below; I can loop in Karthik and Marissa for the deeper evidence pack.

- EU-only routing: If you select an EU execution region we pin inference to EU-hosted nodes; control-plane calls (control APIs for routing decisions) remain in our control plane but are logically separated and do not carry customer payloads. There are no intentional data hops to US compute for the inference payload when EU execution is selected.

- Subprocessors (short):
  - Hosted API: CDN provider (edge ingress), cloud provider compute (managed clusters), logging/observability (vendor X)
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU pools provisioned in your chosen region; we use the same observability tooling but with customer-isolated telemetry streams
  - Private (VPC): optional partner integrator for on-prem install; minimal external subprocessors (provisioning partner, optional monitoring)

- Deletion guarantees: transient request data (in-flight tokens, KV prefixes, and caching) is ephemeral — default TTL is 24 hours for generative cache unless you opt-in to longer retention; upon a customer-initiated deletion request we run a targeted purge pipeline. Typical complete purge timeline for cached inference artifacts is 48–72 hours; control-plane logs that reference routing events are retained per contract and can be shortened with retention settings. Exact SLAs can be added to the contract.

I've kept this intentionally concise. If you want, I'll put together a short evidence packet (SOC2 excerpt, region routing diagram, subprocessors roster) and schedule a 30-min technical walk-through with Karthik next week.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Lead, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@solara.health>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Team <legal@solara.health>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does request data actually run / move?

Vanessa — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our security engineer: 

1) "Control-plane calls remain in our control plane but do not carry customer payloads" — can you confirm any metadata that might be emitted (request path, model id, timing, customer id) and whether that metadata crosses borders when routed? If it does, is it minimized or pseudonymized?

2) For dedicated pools: do you ever perform cross-region failover that would move active workloads to another region without customer opt-in? Need to understand automatic failover behavior.

3) Please include the name/company of the logging/observability provider for hosted customers (we only need vendor names to run procurement checks).

If it helps, we can take the evidence packet then schedule a short call.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@solara.health>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does request data actually run / move?

Alex — hi, Marissa from Trust & Safety (cc: Karthik) — quick answers and enclosed evidence pointers. Attaching SOC2-summary.docx and eu-only-routing-playbook.pdf.

1) Control-plane metadata: we emit minimal routing metadata: model_id (internal alias), region_hint, timestamp, and an opaque customer identifier (never raw customer PII). For EU-execution routes, metadata we send to downstream routing services is pseudonymized and uses region-scoped identifiers; it does not include customer email or tenant name. If you require strict zero-export of any metadata, we offer a Private deployment option where control-plane calls remain on your VPC and we can contract explicit restrictions.

2) Dedicated pools: automatic cross-region failover is opt-in. By default we keep active workloads pinned to the committed region; we will only failover automatically when you select our cross-region resiliency option or in a catastrophic hardware event and after prior agreed notification channels. Failover behavior and RTOs are included in the Dedicated addendum.

3) Observability/logging vendors: hosted telemetry (aggregated) uses LogStream Co for ingestion and AnalyticsHub (vendor) for long-term metrics. For Dedicated we can configure customer-specific telemetry endpoints; logging is separated by tenant and access controls.

Evidence & next steps:
- SOC2-summary.docx (attached) — includes controls around encryption in transit/at rest and subprocessor roster.
- eu-only-routing-playbook.pdf (attached) — step-by-step how a request is pinned to EU nodes and what checks prevent cross-border compute hops.
- redwood_regions_map.pdf (previous attachment) — visual of execution loci and edge ingress.

If you want, Vanessa and I can host a 30-minute technical review with your engineers next Tuesday (09/29 or 10/06 slots free). Let me know preferred time and whether Legal would like a separate conduit for contract-level retention terms.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Trust Engineer, Redwood Inference
